text_nodes.text: League City votes Tuesday on its Flock cameras
Proposition A asks whether police keep plate reader cameras at fixed locations on public roadways. The Tribune reports it is the first such vote in Texas. Drawn to illustrate.
The council leased 42 Flock cameras over two years for up to $233,400, then restated a five year lease of 70 for up to $899,600. One stripe is one camera. Drawn to illustrate.

The 2023 lease covers 70 cameras. Proposition A asks about 55 along public roads, the Tribune reported. A lease and a road count measure different things. Drawn to illustrate.

text_nodes.text: If voters say no, removal is already directed
Resolution No. 2026-185 passed on October 13th with every member on the roll voting For. "There's no second vote needed," Mayor Nick Long said, the Tribune reported. Drawn to illustrate.
72 hours after the count is certified

If voters say no, that is when the city starts bagging the cameras, Long told the council, the Tribune reported. Houston Public Media quoted him on getting them down within 72 hours. One groove for each hour. Drawn to illustrate.

text_nodes.text: Tuesday first, then Kyle and Laredo in May

League City lies in Galveston and Harris counties. Harris County vote centers take voters from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3rd. Kyle and Laredo plan their own votes in May, the Tribune reported. Drawn to illustrate.
